_comment: Ground-truth drift simulator params. Workload split into compute (FLOPs/sec) and memory (bytes) per Sec.5.2.3 updated.

workload._comment: Per-tier workload distributions. Higher tier = more/heavier jobs.
workload._dead_note: sampling_hz and q_cap were never read. Sampling is driven by thermal.T_W_sec and the workload superposition is uncapped.

network._comment: Hockney alpha-beta. alpha in seconds, beta in seconds/byte. THIS IS THE LIVE PAIR: drift_gt.observed_sensor builds link_obs from it, and every DP and cost path reads link_obs. cluster.baseline_link is NOT consulted -- see cluster.py.

_measured.hardware: 2x Jetson Orin Nano 8GB, 25W MAXQ, dedicated 1 GbE (192.168.50.0/24, MTU 1500, no switch), swap off
_measured.method: active probe over edgecolab.transport, framed tensors, the path the migration channel uses; median of 30-40 round trips per size; alpha and beta fitted in separate regimes. tools/measure_link.py
_measured._alpha_is_not_a_link_property: About 174 us of the 487 us alpha is SENDER-SIDE: 137 us CUDA D2H synchronisation (flat across a 16x payload range, so latency not bandwidth) plus ~37 us of host copy, syscalls and header packing. The remainder is wire plus the receiver's ingress path. A CPU-only node would show a different alpha on the same wire.
_measured._homogeneity_assumption: FIRST APPROXIMATION. This pair is Jetson<->Jetson over GbE with THIS transport. The simulator applies one link constant uniformly across an 8-node AGX/NX/Nano cluster, but since a third of alpha is sender-side software and CUDA sync, a different node class genuinely has a different alpha on the same wire -- and alpha_ij is properly per-directed-pair. Adequate for a homogeneous-tier study; revisit before any heterogeneous claim.

_previous_values.note: Simulator OVERSTATED alpha 4.11x and UNDERSTATED beta 4.56x. Opposite directions, and they do not cancel because they dominate at different payload sizes: decode hidden state is alpha-dominated (sim overstated ~3.5-3.8x) while a 16 MiB KV migration is beta-dominated (sim understated ~4.3x).

_paper_5_1_3_says.note: Neither matches the code that produced Table 3. A reproducibility defect independent of accuracy. Note the irony: the paper's stated 300 us is CLOSER to the measured 487 us than the code's 2000 us was -- the text was roughly right and the implementation drifted away from it.

network._degraded_UNMEASURED: degraded_inflation_range is UNMEASURED. It scales the measured normal pair by 2x-3x per the paper's degraded-link description. No degraded link has been measured on the testbed; a congested or contended link may inflate alpha and beta by different factors rather than a common one.

thermal._comment: Asymmetric heating/cooling time constants per tier. GT uses asymmetric; Kalman uses symmetric harmonic mean tau_bar.
thermal._dead_note: use_asymmetric_tau was never read: tau_bar is ALWAYS the harmonic mean of tau_up and tau_down (cluster.Node.tau_bar_s), so the asymmetry is unconditionally collapsed regardless of this flag.

regime._comment: Drift regime toggles. 'default' activates all; others per Sec.5.3.
